So the real opportunity isn’t building a faceless content factory.

You can use AI for research, brainstorming, script development, voice production, visual generation, editing assistance, repurposing, and publishing systems—then add the human layer that makes one channel feel unmistakably different from the thousands of generic channels using the same formula.

That’s especially powerful for entrepreneurs, freelancers, students, content creators, and professionals who have ideas but don’t have hours every day to produce them.

Your AI got approval. Then the work changed. Is that approval still valid?

This is where a lot of AI automation gets too vague.

“Approved” should not be a permanent green light.

A controlled AI approval workflow needs to know:

What action was approved?
Who approved it?
Which version was approved?

Because if the proposal, price, contract language, client commitment, or other material detail changes afterward, the system needs a rule for whether human review is required again.

A button labeled Approve is only useful if the automation reliably respects the decision behind it.

That is the difference between an AI agent that can complete tasks and a governed AI workflow that knows when to stop.

Which business action would you never let AI execute after the underlying information changed without another human review?

name:
Nike Alphafly 4 unboxing 👟

These dropped on Thursday in limited quantities on Nike.com and I happened to have look in the afternoon and grab a size 13 - they sold out moments later.

What’s changed from the v3:

New ZoomX LT foam, 17% lighter than standard ZoomX with 8% more energy return, sitting both above and below the carbon Flyplate. A departure from previous Alphafly architecture rather than a minor tweak.

The Air Zoom pods are now shaped using radio frequency and vibration instead of heat, making them 30% lighter and easier to compress underfoot.

The Flyplate has a more dramatic rocker and a wider base for improved stability, which addresses the main criticism of the v3 for runners who found it unforgiving late in a race.

188g in a men’s size 8.5. 5% lighter than the v3, 10% more energy return. Stack is 39mm heel / 31mm forefoot, 8mm drop. And somehow it’s also slightly cheaper than the v3 was at launch.

First run to follow shortly.

Water pressure problems need the right fix at the source.

A recent Water Tight Canberra job in Farrer involved installing a 20mm pressure limiting valve at the property boundary.

The team excavated around the existing water meter and cold water supply line, altered the line to suit the new pressure limiting valve, installed the valve, then backfilled the area once the work was complete.

A pressure limiting valve helps manage incoming water pressure before it moves through the home’s plumbing system. For Canberra homes, this can be an important part of protecting pipework, taps, fixtures and connected plumbing components from unnecessary pressure strain.

Address- Level 4, Rangs Fortune Square, House 32 Dhanmondi 02, Dhaka 1209

Time 12pm-10pm

Established in the 1980s, another long standing Bangla-Chinese restaurants and one of the oldest in Dhanmondi area. Originally located at Jigatola, the restaurant moved to Dhanmondi 2 few years back and still serves some delicious old school food.

Many people think they closed down because they don’t have any signboards outside the building but they’re still up and running. Ambiance and place/decor is same as other Bangla-Chinese restaurants (plain and simple, nothing special).

Tried some of my favourite from them:
Sizzling Beef- Beef tasted great in terms of flavour and texture but the quantity was poor compared to other places.
756++

Special Thai Soup Thick- Perfect thickness and flavour, good portion of chicken and shrimp. I would generally recommend this but the shrimps’ intestinal tract were not cleaned which is unacceptable, for that reason this is not recommended.
651++

Jing Ling Special Wonton- One of their best items and a must try! They serve 10 pieces with a coriander sauce. Wrapper is crunchy, filling has a mix of chicken and shrimp paired with the super flavourful sauce it’s absolutely amazing. Highly recommended!
651++

Jing Ling Special Fried Rice- Good mix of chicken, shrimp, beef and eggs but it was a bit on the sweet side for my liking.
651++

American Chop Suey- One of my favourites there in general but I got just two pieces of chicken and a shrimp other than veggies in the sauce this time. Not sure if it was the case in my portion or if it was the same with everyone.

Definitely ask the server to serve this on your plate instead of trying to do it yourself (it might get messy if you try).

Underrated must try places!
📍Kabab Village Restaurant

Address- Road 6, House 30, Dhanmondi, Dhaka 1205

Time 1pm-11pm (depending on food availability)

This place has been around over a decade and I have been a loyal customer since the beginning. Even today most people don’t know how good it is especially compared to similar popular places.

They have recently increased their prices though. Also, most of their items get sold out fast especially their only beef item so try to visit by 6pm.

Things I tried:
Chicken grill (quarter) 120
Chicken boti 180
Chicken chaap 150
Beef shikh 200
Chicken reshmi 250
Biscuit naan 100
Butter naan 45
Parata 30

Chicken grill was very well spiced and juicy, it’s underdone sometimes though. Chicken boti is flavourful and solid chicken pieces but it’s not boneless. Their Chicken chaap is very underrated but it’s one of their best items. Their beef shikh is one of my favourites in town, good quantity and has a mustard oil flavour. Chicken reshmi was a hit among all, very creamy-mild flavours unlike other ones but really good.

Biscuit naan is one of their most unique items and something I haven’t tried elsewhere. They use crushed biscuits and powder milk over naan. It’s very sweet so I don’t like it with savoury items instead I have it on its own like dessert.

name:
One of my top 3 sheek kababs in Dhaka!
📍Manzar Kabab

Address- 50/B Zakir Hossain Road, Mohammadpur. Dhaka 1207

Time 5pm-11pm

Total bill at restaurant- BDT 1070

Picture of menus with prices attached at the end.

Such an amazing place for kebabs but it still feels underrated all these years later. This place serves some lip smacking beef items and exceptional beef sheek. The kitchen is open and you can see inside. Keep in mind there are only two small tables to sit at and very long lines. Most people prefer takeaway or eat standing. Also, they have catering services which we have used at family events in case you’re looking for that.

Things I have tried:
Beef sheek kabab BDT 190
Chicken reshmi kabab BDT 150
Chicken hariyali kabab BDT 150
Beef jhaal chaap BDT 250
Beef jhura BDT 250
Reshmi khichuri BDT 160
Beef gosh nehari BDT 250
Beef kabab roll (forgot to take picture and couldn’t find price on menu)
Parata BDT 20

Avoid chicken, go for beef anything that I tried here. Chicken kababs tasted underwhelming with no distinctive flavours. On the contrary, every beef item had prominent flavours. Beef sheek was melt in mouth and so delicious, couldn’t get enough! Beef kabab roll is made using same kabab and their parata with additional onion and chilli. One roll will make you absolutely full because their paratas are gigantic.

While beef jhura was perfect, beef jhaal chaap didn’t seem like it was lightly fried before being cooked in gravy (it’s tasted like a delicious beef gravy though). Reshmi khichuri was jhura beef mixed with rice, very thick and rich, felt more like jhura than khichuri but tasted good. Done expect typical khichuri, I didn’t notice any daal though. Gosh nehari was fantastic! I’m not easily impressed by nehari as most places serve watered down, bland ones but this was thick and flavour packed. I’ll highly recommend the beef items mentioned if you’re confused on what to try at Manzaar.

Legendary Food Places of Dhaka!
📍Chourangi Restaurant

Address- 87, North Brook Hall Road, Bangla Bazar Road, Dhaka 1100

Time 7am-11pm

Established in 1945, this 80 year old eatery was a regular hangout spot for Dhaka’s famous journalists, poets, authors and politicians. They have a small menu serving nasta or morning breakfast and evening snacks consisting of just 4 items each time.

From the very start this place was selling luchi, daal, tea and eggs which is an ongoing tradition. Sometimes they sell aloor dom and bhaji too. Place is pretty small, seating for approximately 24 people. We took 3 eggs 25 taka each- a double mumlet and a single poach, luchi 12 taka each- unlimited free daal with luchi which is a very interesting tradition to keep up even after all these years.

Food was alright- simple and affordable but nothing mind blowing that you must have.

name:
Breakfast Places of Dhaka
📍 Sufi House

Address- Level 10, Rangs Fortune Square, Plot 32, Road 02, Dhanmondi, Dhaka 1209

Time 7am-11pm (breakfast time 7am-12pm)

NB Bill with necessary details attached in post.

If you’re in Dhanmondi and looking for a breakfast spot other than the usual Star kabab or Mughal kabab you might want to check this place. Beef, mutton, chicken and veg options are available with choice of bread plus a dessert. I was going at 12pm (when their breakfast ends) with a group of friends who were going earlier than me. So I messaged the restaurant prior and pre ordered for myself.

When I got there it was chaotic, customers were complaining regarding poor service including my friends. My order came out perfectly whereas my friends complained their food (vegetable korma) wasn’t the same (didn’t have cauliflower unlike mine/as shown on menu). Also, waiters were rude and seemed undertrained.

Coming to the food:

Beef Nehari
Chicken Korma
Vegetable Korma
Mutton Brain Masala
Sweet Lassi
Sufi Special Halwa

Garlic Naan
Luchi
Ghee Parata

Beef nehari broth was rich and flavourful but the nolli quality was average. Chicken korma was alright (1 leg piece cut in two pieces). Veg korma stood out to everyone. Creamy, rich and delicious. Mutton brain masala was very rich, well spiced and delicious. Sweet lassi was perfect- creamy, sweet, balanced. They claimed the halwa was booter dao halwa but none of us could taste that. It was smoother, sweeter. Halwa was rich, sweet and good but not booter dal halwa.

From breads I liked parata most. You may take luchi with halwa but my preference was parata.
